grader_prompt: You are evaluating whether an api skill run produced correct, high-quality output. Review the agent's output text and the commands it executed. For each check below, determine pass/fail and write a one-sentence explanation. Return a JSON object conforming to rubric-schema.json.

checks.description: When hawkop was installed and configured, the agent used hawkop commands (hawkop scan get, hawkop app list, etc.) for the operations hawkop supports, rather than falling back to raw curl.
checks.focus: Commands executed — presence of hawkop vs curl calls

checks.description: The org posture summary is presented as a markdown table with columns: App, Environment, High, Medium, Low, Last Scan. No missing columns, no prose substitution.
checks.focus: Output formatting for Step 3 posture summary

checks.description: Finding counts are broken down by severity (High / Medium / Low) and clearly labeled — not just a single total count.
Every specific scan reference in the output includes an app.stackhawk.com/scans/{scanId} link so the user can drill into evidence directly.
checks.focus: Output links — presence of app.stackhawk.com URLs

checks.description: After presenting results, the agent offered concrete next actions appropriate to the data: drill into High-severity apps, recommend fresh scan for stale apps, direct to platform for triage, or note that low path count may mean coverage gaps.
Apps with lastScanTimestamp older than 30 days were identified and flagged as stale in the posture output.
checks.focus: Step 3 posture summary — stale app detection

checks.description: If any app showed an empty findings list or low path count, the agent flagged this as a potential coverage gap rather than a clean bill of health.
If the user asked about triaging findings, the agent redirected them to the platform UI at app.stackhawk.com rather than attempting triage write operations via API.
checks.focus: Triage guidance — write operation boundary respected
